question:
Which of the following statements about the Indian Desert is/are correct?

1. It lies to the west of the Aravali Hills.

2. It receives an average annual rainfall of over 250 mm.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **Indian Desert**, also known as the **Thar Desert**, is located in the northwestern part of India, mainly in the state of **Rajasthan**.
 
• It lies to the west of the **Aravali Hills**. This is *correct*, as the Thar Desert spans the western regions of Rajasthan, adjacent to the Aravali mountain range.
 
• It receives an average annual rainfall of over **250 mm**. This is *incorrect*. The Indian Desert is an arid region and receives very low annual rainfall, usually in the range of **100-150 mm**.
 
• The climatic conditions in the Indian Desert are characterized by **extreme temperatures**, with hot summers and cold winters, and very little rainfall.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is "Only 1."***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• The **Thar Desert** covers an area of approximately **200,000 square kilometers**, making it the **17th largest desert** in the world and the **9th largest subtropical desert**.
 
• The desert spans the Indian states of **Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana**, as well as parts of southeastern Pakistan.
 
• The Aravali Hills act as a natural barrier, separating the Thar Desert from the more fertile regions of eastern Rajasthan.
 
• The desert's vegetation is sparse, consisting of hardy shrubs and grasses that can survive the arid conditions. Examples include **khejri (Prosopis cineraria)** and **cactus**.
 
• The region relies on **monsoon winds** for rainfall, which is very limited and inconsistent.
 
• The Indian Desert is home to several wildlife species, such as the **Great Indian Bustard**, **Indian Gazelle (Chinkara)**, and various reptiles adapted to desert life.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Indian Desert experiences **extreme diurnal temperatures**. Summers can reach up to **50°C**, while winters can drop to near freezing levels.
 
• The region is known for its **sandy terrain**, with dunes often shifting due to strong winds.
 
• **Water scarcity** is a major issue in the Thar Desert, with many areas dependent on artificial reservoirs or underground water sources.
 
• Famous cities located in the Indian Desert include **Jaisalmer** and **Bikaner**, which are known for their historical and cultural significance.
 
• The **Indira Gandhi Canal** is a key project aimed at providing water for irrigation and drinking purposes in this arid region.
